node-2.label: The patient is a two-year-old boy, the first child of non-consanguineous parents; his mother was a 26-year-old primigravida with no history of spontaneous abortions, stillbirths, or neonatal mortalities, married to a 27-year-old unrelated man

node-3.label: At birth, his weight, length, and occipital-frontal circumference were around the 25th percentile; he had plagiocephaly treated with a cranial band (Care band) worn 23 hours per day until age one, with no skull radiographs taken at that time

attrs.why: Current frontier is 'Genetic bone fragility' (node-8). The skeletal survey findings—cranial/facial hyperostosis (node-11), sclerosed ribs and clavicular hyperostosis (node-12), femoral diaphyseal hyperostosis with stress fractures (node-14), hand dysplasia (node-15), and optic canal narrowing (node-16)—are characteristic of sclerosing skeletal dysplasia. Expert analyses (node-20) favor this over classic OI and other causes, making it the leading more granular refinement of genetic bone fragility.

Juvenile Paget disease is a genetic bone fragility disorder that can present with fractures, hyperostosis, and sclerosis. The pending metabolic labs (node-17), especially ALP, and genetic panel may confirm. It refines 'Genetic bone fragility' but is less likely than sclerosing dysplasia given the specific pattern.
